name: Jerusalem
operatingHours: Light rail Red Line runs ~5:30 AM–~midnight Sunday–Thursday, every ~5–10 min. On Friday service ends ~2–3 PM before Shabbat and resumes Saturday evening ~1 hour after Shabbat ends. The Green Line is opening in stages from 2026–2027; check the operator for current sections.
fareInfo: A single urban ride costs ~₪8 (2025 tariff) and includes free transfers between light rail and city buses for 90 minutes with a Rav-Kav card or a payment app (Rav-Kav Online, Moovit). Rav-Kav cards are sold at the Central Bus Station and light-rail ticket machines. The airport train is a separate Israel Railways fare.

hotels.name: Pontifical Institute Notre Dame of Jerusalem Center
Bezalel Hotel - an Atlas Boutique Hotel

sights.name: Old City of Jerusalem
sights.note: The walled city of under 1 km², divided into Muslim, Christian, Jewish and Armenian quarters and holding sites sacred to all three Abrahamic faiths; enter by Jaffa Gate or Damascus Gate.
sights.hours: Open 24 hours; individual sites keep their own hours

sights.name: Western Wall
sights.note: The surviving retaining wall of the Second Temple platform, Judaism's holiest place of prayer, with a large open plaza and separate men's and women's sections.
sights.hours: Plaza open 24 hours; security check at entrances; modest dress

sights.name: Church of the Holy Sepulchre
sights.note: The church shared by several Christian denominations over the traditional sites of Jesus's crucifixion (Golgotha) and tomb (the Edicule); expect queues for the tomb.
sights.hours: ~5:00 AM–~8:00 PM in summer, to ~7:00 PM in winter

sights.name: Temple Mount / Haram al-Sharif
sights.note: The raised compound holding the Dome of the Rock and Al-Aqsa Mosque; non-Muslim visitors may walk the grounds at set times via the Mughrabi Gate, but not enter the buildings.
sights.hours: Non-Muslim visits ~7:30–11:00 AM and ~1:30–2:30 PM Sun–Thu (shorter in winter); closed Fri, Sat and Muslim holidays; subject to change at short notice

sights.name: Via Dolorosa
sights.note: The processional route of the 14 Stations of the Cross through the Old City lanes, from near Lions' Gate to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.
sights.hours: Open streets; Franciscan procession on Friday afternoons

sights.name: Church of Saint Anne
sights.note: A plain 12th-century Crusader church near Lions' Gate famous for its acoustics, next to the excavated Pools of Bethesda.

sights.name: Tower of David Museum
sights.note: The citadel by Jaffa Gate, now a museum of the city's 4,000-year history with rampart views over the Old City and an evening light show.
sights.hours: ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM Sun–Thu and Sat, to ~2:00 PM Fri

sights.name: City of David
sights.note: An archaeological park on the ridge just south of the Old City walls, with excavations of the ancient city and the walk-through water channel of Hezekiah's Tunnel.
sights.hours: ~8:00 AM–5:00 PM Sun–Thu (to 7:00 PM in summer), to ~2:00 PM Fri; closed Sat

sights.name: Mount of Olives
sights.note: The ridge east of the Old City with the classic panoramic view over the Dome of the Rock and the walls, above the world's oldest continuously used Jewish cemetery.
sights.hours: Viewpoint open all day; churches on the slope keep their own hours

sights.name: Garden of Gethsemane & Church of All Nations
sights.note: Ancient olive trees at the foot of the Mount of Olives, beside the mosaic-fronted Church of All Nations built over the rock where Jesus is said to have prayed.
sights.hours: ~8:00 AM–noon and ~2:30–5:00 PM (to 6:00 PM in summer)

sights.name: The Garden Tomb
sights.note: A quiet garden north of Damascus Gate with a rock-cut tomb that some Protestants consider the burial site of Jesus, run by a British charity.
sights.hours: ~8:30 AM–5:30 PM Mon–Sat; closed Sun except for services

sights.name: Yad Vashem
sights.note: Israel's World Holocaust Remembrance Center on Mount Herzl: a prism-shaped history museum, the Hall of Names and the Children's Memorial. Not suitable for children under 10.
sights.hours: ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM Sun–Thu, to ~2:00 PM Fri; closed Sat and Jewish holidays

sights.name: Israel Museum
sights.note: The national museum, home of the Dead Sea Scrolls in the Shrine of the Book, a 1:50 model of Second Temple-era Jerusalem, and large archaeology and art wings.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM Sun, Mon, Wed, Thu, Sat; 4:00–9:00 PM Tue; 10:00 AM–2:00 PM Fri

sights.name: Mahane Yehuda Market
sights.note: The city's main produce market, loud and crowded before Shabbat, whose shuttered stalls turn into bars and small restaurants at night.
sights.hours: ~8:00 AM–7:00 PM Sun–Thu, to ~3:00 PM Fri, closed Sat; bars open late

sights.name: Ben Yehuda Street
sights.note: The pedestrian spine of downtown West Jerusalem, lined with cafés, souvenir shops and street musicians, busiest on Saturday night after Shabbat.
sights.hours: Open streets; shops ~9:00 AM–late, mostly closed Fri afternoon–Sat

sights.name: Jerusalem Biblical Zoo
sights.note: A large hillside zoo around a lake, focused on animals mentioned in the Bible and endangered species of the region.
sights.hours: ~9:00 AM–6:00 PM Sun–Thu, shorter hours Fri and Sat

sights.name: The First Station
sights.note: The restored Ottoman-era railway terminus turned into an open-air hub of restaurants, weekend events and the start of the Railway Park walking and cycling path.

sights.name: Haas Promenade
sights.note: A stone promenade in Armon HaNatziv with a free sweeping view over the Old City, the Mount of Olives and the Judean Desert, best at sunset.

railStations.name: Jerusalem–Yitzhak Navon
railStations.note: Jerusalem's main rail station, deep underground beside the Central Bus Station: high-speed trains to Ben Gurion Airport (~20 min) and Tel Aviv (~35 min). Connects to the light-rail Red Line at the Central Station stop.
railStations.hours: Trains ~5:30 AM–~midnight Sun–Thu; no service from Friday afternoon until Saturday night (Shabbat).

airports.name: Ben Gurion Airport
airports.transitNote: About 45 km west of Jerusalem. Israel Railways trains from the Terminal 3 station reach Jerusalem–Yitzhak Navon in ~20–25 min (separate fare, ~₪20; not part of the light-rail map), then change to the Red Line. Shared taxis (sherut) run when trains don't, including Shabbat.
airports.hours: Airport–Jerusalem trains ~5:00 AM–~midnight Sun–Thu, every ~30 min; no trains Friday afternoon to Saturday night.
